questions.q: In a normal distribution with mean $\mu = 100$ and $\sigma = 15$, approximately what percentage of scores fall between $70$ and $130$?
questions.answer: $70 = 100 - 2(15)$ and $130 = 100 + 2(15)$. By the Empirical Rule, approximately $95\%$ of data in a normal distribution falls within 2 standard deviations of the mean.

questions.q: Using the 68-95-99.7 rule, what percentage of observations in a normal distribution fall above $\mu + 1\sigma$?
questions.answer: Within 1 standard deviation is $68\%$. The remaining $32\%$ is split evenly between the two tails: $\frac{32\%}{2} = 16\%$ in the upper tail.

questions.q: If heights of adult men are $N(70, 3)$ inches, what percentage are taller than $76$ inches?
questions.answer: $76$ is $70 + 2(3) = \mu + 2\sigma$. Beyond 2 standard deviations is $100\% - 95\% = 5\%$. In the upper tail alone: $\frac{5\%}{2} = 2.5\%$.

questions.q: For a standard normal variable $Z$, find $P(Z < -1.28)$ given that the standard normal CDF at $-1.28$ is approximately $0.10$.
questions.answer: By definition of the cumulative distribution function, $P(Z < -1.28) = 0.10$.

questions.q: A machine fills cereal boxes normally with $\mu = 16.2\text{ oz}$ and $\sigma = 0.1\text{ oz}$. What proportion of boxes contain less than the stated label of $16.0\text{ oz}$?

sections.heading: Section 3: Inverse Normal Calculations (Finding Values from Probabilities)

questions.q: Test scores are normally distributed with $\mu = 500$ and $\sigma = 100$. What score corresponds to the 90th percentile ($z \approx 1.28$)?
In a normal distribution, what are the $z$-scores corresponding to the first quartile ($Q_1$) and third quartile ($Q_3$)?
questions.answer: $Q_1$ has $25\%$ of area below it, giving $z \approx -0.674$. $Q_3$ has $75\%$ below, giving $z \approx +0.674$.

questions.q: The weights of bags of potato chips are $N(\mu, 0.4\text{ oz})$. If the heaviest $5\%$ of bags weigh more than $16.66\text{ oz}$ ($z_{0.95} = 1.645$), find the mean weight $\mu$.

sections.heading: Section 4: Assessing Normality with Normal Probability Plots

questions.q: What appearance in a Normal Probability (Q-Q) Plot indicates that the sample data comes from a roughly normal population?
choices: The plotted points follow a roughly linear pattern
The plotted points form a bell-shaped curve
The plotted points are completely horizontal
The plotted points form a curved parabolic shape
questions.answer: If sample data comes from a normal population, the normal quantile plot displays a straight linear trend.

questions.q: If a Normal Probability Plot shows a clear upward curve (concave up), what does this indicate about the distribution?
choices: The distribution is skewed to the right
The distribution is skewed to the left
questions.answer: A systematic concave-up bend in a normal probability plot indicates right-skewness in the sample data.

questions.q: What is the total area under any valid probability density curve?
questions.answer: By the axioms of probability, the total area under any continuous probability density curve over its entire domain is exactly $1$.
